# Trap Wars - Vendor Evaluation Matrix

## Hard Gates

A candidate cannot advance on weighted score alone. Reject or hold if any answer is no/unclear:

- Commercial game, investor-demo, and promotional use permitted.
- Modification and supported-platform build distribution permitted.
- No unauthorized brand, celebrity, music, training-data, or voice-likeness dependency.
- Required runtime files, dependencies, and rights documents disclosed.
- Vendor accepts a paid evaluation milestone or equivalent low-risk proof.
- Hero and Ray can be delivered as a coherent pair and reach 4/5.
- Unity Humanoid, facial, source/export, and LOD expectations are feasible.

## Weighted Score

Score each criterion 1-5. Weighted points = `score / 5 * weight`. Total is out of 100. A serious finalist needs 75+, no visual criterion below 4, no hard-gate failure, and separate owner visual approval.

| Criterion | Weight | What 5/5 means |
|---|---:|---|
| Visual quality | 18 | Production/investor-ready people, materials, hair, and clothing |
| Character authenticity | 14 | Specific, contemporary, human, and stereotype-free |
| Trap Wars fit | 14 | Naturally belongs with story, world, UI, and progression |
| Facial capability | 10 | Clean required shapes/visemes, eyes/jaw, proven performance |
| Rig quality | 7 | Clean Unity Humanoid, stable hierarchy/bind/scale |
| Animation quality | 5 | Contacts, acting, props, loops, retargeting are production-ready |
| Unity compatibility | 6 | Proven FBX/URP/Mecanim/LOD delivery and support |
| License/rights clarity | 7 | Broad required uses, dependencies disclosed, no ambiguity |
| Revision policy | 3 | Defined rounds, review windows, and change orders |
| Communication | 3 | Clear, timely, technically literate responses |
| Turnaround | 3 | Credible milestone schedule and capacity |
| Cost/value | 4 | Aggregate value is strong, not merely cheap |
| Source-file delivery | 4 | Appropriate editable sources and export manifest included |
| Portfolio relevance | 2 | Comparable grounded people, fashion, face, and game work |
| **Total** | **100** | |

## Approach Pre-Screen

These are routes, not vendor scores. Communication, revisions, portfolio, schedule, and actual visual quality remain unscored until a named proposal and evaluation package exist.

| Approach | Strength | Weakness | Cost class | Expected ceiling | Procurement posture |
|---|---|---|---|---:|---|
| Reallusion/ActorCore foundation plus custom artist | Mature game/facial/LOD ecosystem | License tier and stock-look risk | Moderate-high | 4-5 | Preferred hybrid foundation to quote |
| Custom small studio/artist | Maximum identity/rights control | Portfolio and technical QA variance | High/custom | 5 | Quote alongside hybrid |
| Daz foundation plus technical artist | Broad base/content choice | Interactive licenses and optimization complexity | Moderate-high | 4 | Secondary option only |
| Unity base plus artist | Fastest proof | Source/face/identity ceiling | Low-moderate | 3-4 | Lean fallback; must prove 4/5 |
| ActorCore motion plus custom acting | Efficient locomotion | Stock dialogue risk | Moderate | 4 | Quote with four-clip gate |
| Rokoko/Move AI plus cleanup animator | Fast custom body performance | Capture cleanup/terms | Moderate-high | 4-5 | Evaluate against keyframe quote |
| Custom keyframe/mocap studio | Precise phone and Ray acting | Cost and schedule | High/custom | 5 | Premium motion option |

## Review Record

For every finalist attach portfolio links, quote date/version, license/EULA snapshot, scope, exclusions, dependencies, schedule, revision terms, source list, evaluation contents, weighted worksheet, and owner decision. Never overwrite prior scores; date each revision.
